:::{#thm-entropy-chain-rule-n}
#### Chain rule for entropy, many variables

For [discrete random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X_1, \ldots, X_n$
with finite entropies, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

$$H(X_1, \ldots, X_n) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} H(X_i \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1}),$$

where the term for $i = 1$ is $H(X_1)$. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

:::

::: {.proof}

The proof is by induction on $n$.
The claim for $n = 1$ is $H(X_1) = H(X_1)$.

Suppose the claim holds for $n - 1$ variables.
Treat $(X_1, \ldots, X_{n-1})$ as one discrete random variable.
The [chain rule](#thm-entropy-chain-rule) for two variables gives

$$H(X_1, \ldots, X_n) = H(X_1, \ldots, X_{n-1}) + H(X_n \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{n-1}).$$

The induction hypothesis expands the first term on the right:

$$
\begin{aligned}
H(X_1, \ldots, X_n)
&= \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} H(X_i \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1}) + H(X_n \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{n-1}) \\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{n} H(X_i \mid X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1}).
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
